title: SEQUENCE
description: Learn how to use SEQUENCE objects to generate a sequence of numeric values in SQL Server.

data.text: A SEQUENCE is a user-defined schema-bound object that generates a sequence of numbers according to a specified specification. Unlike IDENTITY columns, sequences are not associated with a table and can be shared across multiple tables.

data.title: CREATE SEQUENCE Syntax
data.content: Creates a sequence object with configurable options.
data.code:
CREATE SEQUENCE [schema_name.] sequence_name
    [ AS integer_type ]
    [ START WITH start_value ]
    [ INCREMENT BY increment_value ]
    [ { MINVALUE [ min_value ] } | { NO MINVALUE } ]
    [ { MAXVALUE [ max_value ] } | { NO MAXVALUE } ]
    [ CYCLE | { NO CYCLE } ]
    [ { CACHE [ cache_size ] } | { NO CACHE } ];

data.text: Using a Sequence with a Table
Sequences can be used to generate values for table columns, especially useful when you need the sequence value before inserting.

data.title: SEQUENCE Key Points
points: SEQUENCE objects generate numeric values independently of tables.
Sequences can be shared across multiple tables.
Use NEXT VALUE FOR to get the next sequence value.
Sequences support cycling, caching, and configurable min/max values.
Sequences are more flexible than IDENTITY columns for advanced scenarios.
